Issued at 111 AM EST Thu Nov 26 2026

Pattern / Forecast Synopsis: 

Textbook inland runner cyclone setup well underway across the eastern 
1/3 of NOAM. An absolute unit of a 1043mb surface high remains 
anchored over Atlantic Canada and into Maine / southern Quebec, 
providing a dominant blocking mechanism for phasing, moisture rich 
system over the far southeastern CONUS. Racing 160kt jet streak 
stretching from Florida through Atlantic Canada to help drive robust 
surface cyclogenesis within aforementioned jet streak's right 
entrance region... eventually culminating in a pseudo pinwheeling / 
cutoff 985-995mb surface low that initially stalls in the vicinity 
of Cleveland tonight into Friday, but should suffice in nosing deep 
enough theta-e advection into the far southeastern reaches of the 
CWA. 

Despite the borderline cutoff nature of the system, blocking 
mechanism over Atlantic Canada to quickly break down as zippy split 
progressive flow within both the northern and southern stream 
manifests to force this eventually mature system into Atlantic 
Canada by Friday night into Saturday. Result for the weekend and 
beyond will be a smattering of moisture-starved northern stream 
waves racing along the periphery of a flattening longwave trough 
anchoring itself over Hudson Bay through the weekend, while another 
potent Pacific borne wave ejects into the Plains, eventually being 
ingested by the southern stream across the Tennessee Valley Sunday 
into Monday (hence the moisture starvation of the northern stream 
waves). Once that wave clears, height rises commence into next week 
amid more zippy progressive northern stream flow across the northern 
CONUS... with additional moisture starved waves making a run at the 
region closer to midweek next week. 

Details:

Aforementioned moisture rich system to struggle to intrude into the 
region as residual subsidence leftover from the departing surface 
high pressure fails to allow for any moderation of the low levels of 
the atmosphere. Ample moisture intrusion aloft will lead to 
generally overcast skies for most for the Thanksgiving holiday, 
though with such a dry airmass in the mid and low levels to gobble 
up any moisture intrusion in those layers of the atmosphere, 
anticipation is that ALL of APX-Land squeaks out a dry Turkey Day 
with highs well into the 40s. The one caveat to all of this is that 
with the deepening surface low coupled with such a strong area of 
high pressure, the pressure gradient will become increasingly 
pinched through the day today, peaking tonight... especially south 
of the Big Bridge. As such, rather blustery winds straight out of 
the northeast to manifest with time today across northern lower 
(strongest along Lake Huron south of Alpena, where some 25 to 35mph+ 
gusts will be possible), with wind speeds peaking this evening into 
early tonight. 

This will also coincide with the most efficient area of lift nosing 
into the region, allowing for precipitation to manifest across 
northeast lower, despite the deepest moisture generally getting 
bottled up just southeast of the Saginaw Bay region. Current trends 
continue to favor an overwhelming majority of precipitation to favor 
areas along and east of a Lake City to Cheboygan line. Two primary 
talking points with this system to address here... the first of 
course being precipitation amounts through Friday. In the 
aforementioned highlighted region, the farther west one goes, QPF 
likely holds below 0.05". In contrast, the area where the greatest 
precip is anticipated generally favors the Lake Huron / Saginaw Bay 
counties from Alcona to Arenac. Latest hi-res data is beginning to 
showcase potential for a brief intrusion of deeper moisture into the 
aforementioned counties, and thus potential for QPF as high as 0.75" 
in the event this more efficient zone of rainfall can manifest later 
tonight into Friday. With so much dry air into play, we will be 
walking a meteorological tightrope, as a pretty stout QPF gradient 
to manifest the farther west one goes from the lakeshore. Entirely 
possible lakeshore locales in the aforementioned counties see 
significantly more QPF than areas just 5-10mi inland. For those in 
NW lower and eastern upper actually still reading this, anticipation 
is that this system will be a clean miss for you, with maybe a 
sprinkle or two at most. 

The other story is the potential for snow across interior northern 
lower. Before anyone goes into full-on panic mode, will mention 
there is a lot working against this idea. However, through the 
process of evaporative cooling / wet-bulbing within the low levels 
of the atmosphere, entirely possible that any pockets of steadier 
precip throw some wet snowflakes (or sleet pellets as the 850mb wet 
bulb temp is going to hover right at or just above 0C). All in 
all, there is such little moisture concentration across the
